data.title: Single checkpoint plan gains ground
data.description: Thailand and Laos have discussed introducing a single inspection checkpoint for customs and immigration procedures to streamline cross-border trade and strengthen regional connectivity.

data.title: MP Suchada under House scrutiny
data.description: Bhumjaithai MP Suchada Zhang Thaensap, 33, has come under parliamentary scrutiny following allegations involving her husband and cryptocurrency transactions.

data.title: Veteran Worawut to lead boccia team at Para Games
data.description: Three-time world champion Worawut Saengampa will lead Thailand's boccia team at the forthcoming Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, which run from 18 to 24 Oct.

data.title: Two hurt in petrol station blast
data.description: Narathiwat: A bomb exploded at a PT petrol station in Tak Bai district on Thursday night, damaging fuel pumps and the station building and injuring two employees, authorities said.

data.title: Alarm as tobacco firms target Asean
data.description: Public health advocates have sounded the alarm over aggressive interference by multinational tobacco companies in Southeast Asia, warning that without stronger regional safeguards, millions of lives remain at risk.

data.title: Chinese suspect held over drug trafficking network
data.description: A Chinese man suspected of helping a transnational drug trafficking network ship drugs from Thailand to China has been arrested in Bangkok.

data.title: More rain coming from Oct 11-14
data.description: The government has warned residents in the Central Plains and areas along the Chao Phraya River to prepare for heavy rain expected on Oct 11-14 as authorities continue flood relief and water-management operations.

data.title: New Supreme Court chief pledges fairer access to justice
data.description: Weerapong Sudawong, the 52nd president of the Supreme Court, has pledged to uphold the rule of law, widen access to justice and keep the judicial process from being distorted as he set out policies for fiscal 2027.

data.title: City steps up drainage before rains
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) is accelerating efforts to drain floodwater in the Saphan Sung and Lat Krabang areas ahead of rainfall forecast for Oct 5-8.

data.title: Brazil election debate chaos sparks censorship row
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO (BRAZIL) - Brazil's judiciary came under fire Friday for sparking the cancellation of an election debate by meddling in its rules after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva refused to attend.

data.title: Argentina unveils passports-for-investment scheme
data.description: BUENOS AIRES (ARGENTINA) - Argentine President Javier Milei's government said Friday that the country would offer citizenship to foreigners who invest at least $350,000 in the country.

data.title: King Charles to evoke colonial 'darkest days' on Caribbean tour
data.description: LONDON - King Charles III will acknowledge the "darkest days" of colonial rule and slavery while touring Caribbean countries on a visit beginning this month, a Buckingham Palace spokesperson said Friday.

data.title: Bhumjaithai MP faces questions over finances
data.description: People’s Party MP Rangsiman Rome will invite Bhumjaithai MP Suchada Zhang Thaensap and her husband to clarify cryptocurrency and financial transactions on Oct 7.

data.title: Russia ‘tearing Kyiv apart’, mayor says
data.description: KYIV - Russian attacks on key infrastructure were “tearing Kyiv apart”, the city’s mayor said Friday, as strikes on a bridge linking the capital’s east and west brought traffic to a standstill.

data.title: China widens military footprint with Laos air base
data.description: BANGKOK - When China opened its first overseas air force base this week, a joint facility in isolated Laos, it was sending a signal — its foreign military foothold is set to grow, analysts say.

data.title: Tigray conflict puts Ethiopia at odds with neighbours
data.description: ADDIS ABABA - Ethiopia’s Tigray rebels have been pushed out of a neighbouring state by a government counter-offensive, a humanitarian source said Friday, but the conflict has triggered a breakdown in the country’s relations with Eritrea and Egypt.

data.title: Bhumjaithai seeks to reform Thai PBS funding
data.description: The Bhumjaithai Party has proposed overhauling the way Thai Public Broadcasting Service (Thai PBS) is funded by scrapping its earmarked share of alcohol and tobacco taxes, worth up to 2 billion baht a year, and making annual government budget allocations its main source of funding.

data.title: Baggage claims to be moved to new location, THAI compensation pledged
data.description: Thai Airways International (THAI) will move baggage collection to a new place on Saturday as the Ministry of Transport has pledged financial compensation for flyers affected by flight and baggage chaos after flooding paralysed the airline.

data.title: Swiss president to quit government
data.description: GENEVA - Swiss President Guy Parmelin announced on Friday that he will quit the government at the end of the year, in a sudden move after more than a decade of ministerial service.

data.title: WHO: Life expectancy almost back to pre-Covid levels
data.description: GENEVA - Global life expectancy is close to the levels seen before the Covid-19 pandemic, but the outlook for years lived in good health is recovering more slowly, the World Health Organization said on Friday.

data.title: Man City launch appeal against explosive financial ruling
data.description: MANCHESTER - Manchester City confirmed on Friday that they had launched an appeal against a damning judgement that found the club guilty of more than 100 charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules.

data.title: Three more golds help Thailand surpass target
data.description: Thailand’s women made a splash on the water and a statement on the sand and in the boxing ring at the Asian Games, as a three-gold haul on Friday took the Kingdom to 15 golds in Aichi-Nagoya, one better than its target of 14.

data.title: Spain housing reform vote pending as protests mount
data.description: MADRID - Spain’s parliament was to vote Friday on government housing decrees introduced after nationwide protests triggered by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, but there were doubts the measures would pass.

data.title: Swedish Social Democrats try again to form government
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Sweden’s parliament speaker said on Friday that he had asked Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson to make a new attempt to form a government, days after a first bid failed.
